correctness.rationale: The local CRT factors are exact: for any odd q not dividing h precisely ±h are two distinct invertible forbidden classes mod q², while q dividing h forbids none for p≠q. PNT in a fixed progression proves each truncated density; Brun--Titchmarsh bounds q≤X^1/4 and elementary all-integer counting bounds larger squares, giving a vanishing normalized tail. The Euler product converges absolutely. Finite first-factor and tail inequalities prove C>1/2; removing q=3 yields sharp separated bands, with primorial limits showing both upper endpoints optimal. A standalone verifier independently checked 225 local residue cases and nine exact CRT cases, plus 49,071 sample primes. It did not infer an infinite theorem from samples.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary paper proves only the one-step joint-flat density (Theorem 8) and explicitly presents the general fixed odd-shift dichotomy as a numerical observation requiring investigation (comment immediately after Corollary 10, p. 290). The new claim has an h-dependent correction for every odd prime dividing h and a proved sharp uniform ternary separation; these are not supplied by its published h=1 statement. Actual published-record searches and recoverable prior claims yielded no dominating theorem. A general unindexed sieve theorem could subsume the formula, so publication priority is not certified.

value.rationale: The 2010 primary source specifically highlights the unexplained observed greater-than-half density for every odd shift and the markedly higher regime when 3 divides the shift. The proof resolves the observation exactly for all fixed odd shifts, shows an absolute separation of the two regimes (at most 2/3 versus greater than 3/4), gives all equality and limiting extremal cases, and identifies the prime-support invariant controlling densities. This is a motivated full structural classification of the shifted density, not an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
